When to Involve Your Funding Agency

From the ORA eTraining module "Post Award Quick Guide" (lesson 6 of 9).
Actions That May Require Prior Approval
While the PI has substantial latitude in executing the project, if there are changes to the initial plan, there are several items that may need prior approval from the funding agency. These items vary by the funding agency, and the Notice of Award, and may also change over the years. PI Handbook #3: Grant-Related Processes pages 58 – 64 has further details about "Deviations from the Original Plan." For example, NIH: the NIH may allow the PI to move substantial amounts of funds between budget lines (for example, from travel to supplies); indeed, moving up to 25% of funds is generally allowable for NIH awards. In fact, for the NIH, even more may be allowable as long as there is no change in scope. If you are not sure if the change you seek is allowable under your award, please email ask.ora@morgan.edu and be sure to include details about the suggested change and a copy of the Notice of Award.
Some salient examples of change in scope are: "Change in the specific aims approved at the time of award; Substitution of one animal model for another; Change from the approved use of live vertebrate animals; Change from the approved involvement of human subjects that would result in an increased risk…" For further information on the NIH's definition of the change of scope, please click here .

When to Involve Your Funding Agency
The table below shows some examples of items that USUALLY require prior approval. This is agency-dependent so please be sure to check with your funding agency and NOA.

Change Sought Agency Documentation Reviewed* NOA Reviewed ORA Reviewed Is Prior Approval Required? Change of PI (or substantial reduction/addition of time and effort) Change of key personnel (or substantial reduction/addition of time and effort) Change of the scope of work Substantially changing or modifying specific aims Reallocating budget across budget lines Transferring any funds from Participant Support Costs (Line 12) Changing or adding cost share Changing or adding a Subaward Adding or changing work with vertebrate animals or human subjects Applying new and unapproved technology Adding a foreign (i.e. non-USA) component Purchasing equipment not previously listed in the budget Carry over of funds No cost extension Transferring the award from one institution to another Early termination or relinquishment
*Agency documentation can often be found online. Examples include: NIH'S Grant Policy Statement (NIH GPS) , NSF's Proposal & Award Policies & Procedures Guide (PAPPG) , NASA's Grant and Cooperative Agreement Manual (GCAM)

Knowledge check: Which if the following is NOT a typical example of an action that requires prior approval from your funding agency?
  - No-Cost Extension  [incorrect]
  - Adding a subaward  [incorrect]
  - Adding an additional 20% of funding to a student contract  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - Purchasing equipment not previously mentioned in the budget justification  [incorrect]
